---
name: meeting-minutes
description: Turn internal meeting transcripts of up to 60 minutes into concise decisions and action items with evidence locations.
---
# Meeting minutes

Use an actual transcript, agenda or supplied notes. If only audio exists, first use audio-transcription within its actual supported runtime limits; the audio must also fit the source-size and codec limits documented by that runtime.

Record available meeting metadata, attendees and source identity. Missing details are Unknown; ask only for information that materially blocks the requested result. Draft from evidence using references/template.md: summary, decisions, action items, unresolved questions and source references. A suggestion is not an approved decision. Deferred, postponed, or not-decided is not rejected: never rewrite “no decision today” as refusal, rejection, or cancellation. Check the summary and every detailed section separately against the same source; a correct table does not repair an unsupported summary claim. A mentioned person is not automatically an action owner. Unknown owners and dates remain Unknown. Each decision/action links to its original quote, segment or actual time range; do not invent word-level timestamps.

Keep short meetings concise. Review every significant claim against source text; label corrections or ambiguity. Produce the requested Markdown/Word/PDF using existing file and Office capabilities. Open/render actual files before publication. Use wx_artifact_publish and wait for existing writeback. Publishing a file here does not authorize external distribution, emails or creating tasks; those require separate user intent and actual tools.

Read references/upstream.md for adaptation and scope. No automatic sharing, ASR engine or new task system is included.

# Minutes template

Title / date / duration / organizer / attendees: factual values or Unknown.
Source: attachment identity, original hash or supplied notes; state missing evidence.

## Summary
Meeting objective and supported outcome in one short paragraph.

## Decisions
Decision; approving person/group if explicit; rationale; original quote and segment/range. Clearly distinguish proposed and confirmed decisions.

## Action items
Action; owner or Unknown; due date or Unknown; acceptance criterion if explicit; evidence location. Do not silently turn a discussion topic into an assigned task.

## Agenda notes and unresolved questions
Brief factual notes, blockers and questions. Suggested next steps must be labelled suggestions.

## References and revision
Actual sources only, draft revision and substantive corrections. For ≤30-minute meetings aim for about one page; for ≤60-minute meetings about two pages when content permits. Layout preferences never justify dropping important decisions.
